To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the choice of sex act, the use of condoms, and the HIV test status of the sexual partner each have a major influence on the relative risk of acquiring HIV during sex.

The per-act risk for HIV infection varies substantially by sex act (anal intercourse > oral sex > vaginal sex > receptive fellatio > insertive fellatio) and by condom use (unprotected sex > condoms > female condoms > male condoms).

(1) choosing a partner who tested HIV-negative instead of an un-tested partner, using condoms, and choosing insertive oral sex instead of insertive anal sex all reduce the per-act risk for HIV infection substantially, and (2) the absolute risk reduction associated with choosing a partner who has tested HIV-negative is much smaller for men who have anal sex with men than for heterosexuals.
